sources.title: Metformin for metastatic prostate cancer: STAMPEDE randomized phase 3 trial
sources.preview: Adding metformin did not significantly improve overall survival in the full metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate-cancer population, but reduced adverse metabolic effects of androgen deprivation.
sources.population: 1,874 participants without diabetes and with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer

sources.title: Addition of metformin to concurrent chemoradiation in locally advanced non-small-cell lung cancer
sources.preview: Adding metformin to chemoradiation did not improve survival in unresectable stage III non-small-cell lung cancer.
sources.population: People without diabetes and with unresectable stage III NSCLC

sources.title: Metformin with chemoradiotherapy in locally advanced NSCLC: OCOG-ALMERA
sources.preview: Metformin did not improve outcomes and was associated with worse survival estimates in this small trial.
sources.population: Patients with locally advanced non-small-cell lung cancer

sources.title: Metformin for chemoprevention of recurrent colorectal adenoma or polyps
sources.preview: Low-dose metformin reduced adenoma and polyp recurrence at one year after polypectomy in patients without diabetes.
sources.population: 151 randomized patients after colorectal polyp removal; 133 had one-year colonoscopy

sources.title: Metformin suppresses colorectal aberrant crypt foci in a short-term clinical trial
sources.preview: Metformin reduced colorectal epithelial proliferation and rectal aberrant crypt foci in this short trial.
sources.population: Patients without diabetes with colorectal aberrant crypt foci

sources.title: Metformin induces autophagy and cell-cycle arrest in myeloma by targeting AMPK and mTOR
sources.preview: Metformin inhibited myeloma-cell growth with AMPK activation and mTORC1/mTORC2 inhibition.
sources.population: Human myeloma cell lines and NOD-SCID mouse xenografts

guides.title: Metformin
guides.description: How metformin works, its investigated benefits across infections, cancer, neurological conditions and physical function, and its safety.

sections.label: Overview
sections.title: What is metformin?
sections.paragraph: Metformin is an oral medicine for type 2 diabetes. Researchers are also investigating its effects on Parkinson’s disease, cognition in schizophrenia, age-related muscle loss and Long COVID. These investigations examine different possible benefits, from preserving nerve-cell function and changing energy metabolism to reducing viral replication during an infection.

sentences.text: Metformin is an oral medicine for type 2 diabetes.
Researchers are also investigating its effects on Parkinson’s disease, cognition in schizophrenia, age-related muscle loss and Long COVID.
These investigations examine different possible benefits, from preserving nerve-cell function and changing energy metabolism to reducing viral replication during an infection.

sections.label: Benefits
sections.paragraph: The benefits being investigated include reducing Long COVID risk, improving cognition in schizophrenia, preserving physical function in older adults and improving Parkinson’s symptoms. A small schizophrenia trial reported improved cognitive-test scores with metformin, while the Parkinson’s pilot and the MET-PREVENT sarcopenia trial did not demonstrate improvements in their main clinical outcomes. For Long COVID, COVID-OUT reported a prevention signal, although a correction notice and inconsistent control percentages complicate interpretation; ACTIV-6 did not meet its primary efficacy threshold, and a separate trial found no improved recovery after symptoms were established. Cancer trials have generally not demonstrated the hoped-for treatment benefits; a separate colorectal study found fewer recurrent adenomas after polyp removal, which is a prevention outcome.

questions.question: Does metformin improve symptoms of Parkinson’s disease?
questions.answer: A three-month pilot randomized 60 people to metformin or placebo alongside levodopa/carbidopa. Clinical scores improved within the metformin group, but the comparison between groups did not show a statistically significant benefit on the total Unified Parkinson’s Disease Rating Scale. The trial was small, used a per-protocol analysis and was too short to establish whether metformin slows disease progression.

The trial was small, used a per-protocol analysis and was too short to establish whether metformin slows disease progression.

questions.question: What has the schizophrenia research found about cognition?
questions.answer: In a 72-person open-label randomized trial, adding metformin to antipsychotic treatment improved the composite cognitive-test score by an estimated 3.43 points more than antipsychotics alone after 24 weeks (95% CI 1.83–5.02). The participants were predominantly young adults, 59 completed follow-up, and the study lacked a placebo group; larger blinded studies are needed to confirm the size and practical importance of this effect. A later analysis of the same trial linked changes in metabolites and hippocampal connectivity with cognitive changes.

questions.question: Does metformin improve muscle strength or physical function?
questions.answer: The 2025 MET-PREVENT trial randomized 72 older adults with probable sarcopenia and prefrailty or frailty to metformin or placebo for four months. It found no walking-speed benefit: the adjusted difference was 0.001 m/s (95% CI −0.06 to 0.06), and metformin was poorly tolerated in this population. The 2023 review described inconsistent results: some research suggested faster walking, but strength outcomes were not consistently improved and exercise adaptations could be reduced. In the MASTERS trial, adding metformin to resistance training reduced muscle growth in healthy older adults; the difference in strength gains was not statistically significant.

questions.question: Does taking metformin during COVID-19 prevent Long COVID?
questions.answer: COVID-OUT reported fewer later clinician-diagnosed cases when treatment began during acute infection, but the estimate remains provisional because the report contains inconsistent control percentages and has a published correction. ACTIV-6 examined symptoms attributed to COVID-19 or death at six months and did not meet its prespecified threshold for benefit. The trials enrolled different populations and used different outcomes, leaving uncertainty about how much prevention benefit metformin provides.

questions.question: Does metformin help when Long COVID is already established?
questions.answer: A randomized South Korean trial did not find improved recovery after a two-week course of metformin in people with persistent symptoms. That result concerns the population and short treatment course tested; it does not establish the effect of longer courses or treatment in every Long COVID subgroup. A separate metformin-and-fluvoxamine fatigue report was retracted and republished; its original findings cannot serve as reliable evidence of metformin benefit.

questions.question: What did the acute COVID-19 trial show?
questions.answer: COVID-OUT did not meet its primary composite endpoint combining hypoxemia, emergency-department attendance, hospitalization or death. That acute endpoint is separate from later Long COVID diagnosis.

questions.question: Does metformin improve prostate-cancer survival?
questions.answer: STAMPEDE randomized 1,874 men with metastatic hormone-sensitive disease. Overall survival did not improve significantly: hazard ratio 0.91, 95% CI 0.80–1.03. Adverse metabolic effects of androgen deprivation were reduced.

questions.question: Does adding metformin help in lung cancer?
questions.answer: NRG-LU001 found no survival improvement with metformin added to chemoradiation. OCOG-ALMERA also found no benefit and reported worse survival estimates in the metformin group.

sentences.text: NRG-LU001 found no survival improvement with metformin added to chemoradiation. OCOG-ALMERA also found no benefit and reported worse survival estimates in the metformin group.

questions.question: Did metformin prevent breast-cancer recurrence?
questions.answer: In MA.32, metformin did not improve invasive disease-free survival when added to standard care in patients without diabetes. In the hormone-receptor-positive primary analysis, the hazard ratio was 1.01, 95% CI 0.84–1.21.

questions.question: Is the colorectal finding about cancer treatment or prevention?
questions.answer: It concerns prevention of recurrent adenomas and polyps after removal. In the one-year trial, adenoma recurrence was lower with 250 mg daily metformin, with a reported risk ratio of 0.60, 95% CI 0.39–0.92. Survival after established cancer was not the endpoint.

questions.question: Does metformin improve pancreatic-cancer survival?
questions.answer: Adding metformin to gemcitabine and erlotinib did not improve survival in a 121-person trial: overall-survival hazard ratio 1.056, 95% CI 0.72–1.55.

questions.question: What benefit has been shown in multiple myeloma research?
questions.answer: The cited experiment found slower myeloma-cell and xenograft growth. It tested cell cultures and mice, so it provides an experimental finding rather than a measured patient benefit.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: Metformin commonly causes diarrhoea, nausea and abdominal discomfort; longer use can lower vitamin B12. Its major serious risk is lactic acidosis, particularly with impaired kidney function, hypoxia, liver disease or excessive alcohol intake.

sentences.text: Metformin commonly causes diarrhoea, nausea and abdominal discomfort; longer use can lower vitamin B12.
Its major serious risk is lactic acidosis, particularly with impaired kidney function, hypoxia, liver disease or excessive alcohol intake.

questions.question: What monitoring is relevant?
questions.answer: Kidney function and vitamin B12 are relevant monitoring targets; certain contrast scans, surgery or acute hypoxic illness can require temporary interruption.

sentences.text: Kidney function and vitamin B12 are relevant monitoring targets; certain contrast scans, surgery or acute hypoxic illness can require temporary interruption.

questions.question: What did the Long COVID prevention trial report about safety?
questions.answer: ACTIV-6 found no safety concern for its selected low-risk adult population, but monitored lactic acidosis and medically diagnosed hypoglycaemia rather than comprehensively measuring tolerability.

sentences.text: ACTIV-6 found no safety concern for its selected low-risk adult population, but monitored lactic acidosis and medically diagnosed hypoglycaemia rather than comprehensively measuring tolerability.

sections.label: Contraindications
sections.paragraph: Contraindications include eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m², metabolic acidosis and metformin hypersensitivity; starting treatment at eGFR 30–45 is not recommended.

sentences.text: Contraindications include eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m², metabolic acidosis and metformin hypersensitivity; starting treatment at eGFR 30–45 is not recommended.

sections.label: Interactions
sections.paragraph: Insulin or sulfonylureas increase hypoglycaemia risk; topiramate can increase acidosis risk; cimetidine, dolutegravir and ranolazine can increase metformin exposure. Excessive alcohol also increases lactic-acidosis risk.

sentences.text: Insulin or sulfonylureas increase hypoglycaemia risk; topiramate can increase acidosis risk; cimetidine, dolutegravir and ranolazine can increase metformin exposure.
Excessive alcohol also increases lactic-acidosis risk.

sections.label: Dosing
sections.title: What schedules have repurposing trials tested?
sections.paragraph: The COVID-OUT and ACTIV-6 prevention trials tested a 14-day course of immediate-release metformin, increasing to 1,500 mg daily. The Parkinson’s pilot used 500 mg twice daily for three months, while the schizophrenia trial used up to 1,500 mg daily for 24 weeks. These studies tested different treatment schedules for different conditions; they did not establish one repurposing dose or demonstrate equivalent outcomes with extended-release metformin.

sections.label: Results
sections.paragraph: In the schizophrenia trial, the between-group difference in the composite cognitive-test score was 3.43 points at 24 weeks (95% CI 1.83–5.02). MET-PREVENT found a walking-speed difference of 0.001 m/s at four months (95% CI −0.06 to 0.06). The South Korean Long COVID trial reported recovery in 84 of 132 participants receiving metformin (63.6%) and 90 of 132 receiving placebo (68.2%) at eight weeks.

sections.label: Quality
sections.paragraph: FDA-approved generic medicines must match the reference product’s active ingredient, strength, dosage form and route, and demonstrate bioequivalence. Release formulation also matters: the Long COVID prevention trials described here used immediate-release metformin and did not compare it with an extended-release product.

sections.label: Status
sections.paragraph: The U.S. prescribing information lists metformin as an adjunct to diet and exercise for type 2 diabetes in adults and children aged 10 years and older. Parkinson’s disease, schizophrenia, sarcopenia and Long COVID are investigated uses rather than indications listed in that prescribing information.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: COVID-OUT has a published correction notice and conflicting control-group percentages in the available report. Its long-term diagnosis estimate should be read with that qualification. The original REVIVE fatigue report has a notice of retraction and republication; its original results are not used as evidence of benefit.

faqs.question: Do immediate-release and extended-release metformin have the same evidence for Long COVID?
faqs.answer: The prevention trials used immediate-release metformin. They did not compare release formulations, so their results do not establish equal Long COVID outcomes for an extended-release product.

faqs.question: Is a short course during COVID-19 the same as treating established Long COVID?
faqs.answer: No. Prevention trials start treatment during the acute infection and measure later illness, whereas the South Korean treatment trial enrolled people who already had persistent symptoms.

originalUse.text: Oral treatment to improve glucose control in type 2 diabetes.

originalAction.text: Metformin reduces glucose production by the liver and intestinal glucose absorption, while helping tissues take up and use glucose more effectively. It improves the response to insulin without stimulating insulin secretion.

summary.text: These effects on glucose handling sit alongside actions on cellular energy sensing, inflammation and protein processing—the pathways being investigated in neurological disease, muscle ageing and COVID-19.

questions.title: Why is metformin being investigated for Long COVID?
questions.text: One proposed route is suppression of mTOR, a host-cell pathway involved in making proteins that SARS-CoV-2 needs to reproduce. In the COVID-OUT trial’s nasal-swab study, metformin reduced the average viral RNA level during acute infection compared with placebo. This supports investigating whether reducing the early viral burden changes the risk of later illness; starting treatment after Long COVID has developed addresses a separate question.

questions.title: Why is metformin being investigated for Parkinson’s disease?
questions.text: The rationale is to protect dopamine-producing nerve cells by changing inflammation and the removal of damaged cellular material. In mouse and cell experiments, metformin activated the energy sensor AMPK and autophagy, the cell’s recycling process, while reducing mitochondrial oxidative stress and accumulation of alpha-synuclein protein. The human pilot investigated this approach alongside levodopa/carbidopa and measured symptoms together with blood markers of inflammation and nerve-cell biology.

questions.title: How might metformin affect cognition in schizophrenia?
questions.text: The proposed connection is energy metabolism: the tricarboxylic acid cycle helps cells convert nutrients into usable energy, including in brain networks involved in memory. An exploratory study linked changes in blood metabolites during metformin treatment with changes in working memory, verbal learning and hippocampal brain connectivity. These associations identify a possible explanation for cognitive changes; the study did not directly measure energy production inside the brain.

questions.title: Why is metformin being investigated for muscle ageing and sarcopenia?
questions.text: Researchers have tested whether metformin’s effects on inflammation and energy sensing could preserve muscle or improve its response to exercise. Those pathways can have competing effects: AMPK activation may also restrain mTORC1 signaling, which supports muscle growth. In the MASTERS trial, older adults taking metformin during resistance training gained less lean and thigh muscle mass than those taking placebo.

questions.title: Why study metformin during androgen deprivation?
questions.text: Androgen deprivation can worsen metabolic health. STAMPEDE tested whether metformin could reduce those effects and improve cancer outcomes; metabolic outcomes improved without a significant overall survival benefit.

questions.title: Why has metformin been tested alongside lung-cancer treatment?
questions.text: Investigators tested the preclinical hypothesis that altering tumor metabolism could increase sensitivity to chemoradiation. The two randomized studies did not confirm the expected clinical benefit.

questions.title: What was the proposed mechanism in breast cancer?

questions.title: What was the rationale in pancreatic cancer?
questions.text: Researchers proposed that metformin could create metabolic stress in tumor cells and modify insulin-related growth signals. The randomized trial tested that rationale alongside chemotherapy and found no survival improvement.

questions.title: Which pathways changed in the myeloma experiments?
questions.text: In cell lines and mouse xenografts, metformin activated AMPK and suppressed mTORC1 and mTORC2 signaling, with autophagy and cell-cycle arrest. These changes accompanied reduced tumor-cell growth.
